bounded_slice.candidate: RFC 6920 Named Information hash-algorithm identifiers as a standalone digest-identity binding for an evidence envelope

primary_source.title: RFC 6920: Naming Things with Hashes
inspected_sections: 9.4 Creation of Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry

bounded_slice.tested_scope: Static inspection of exactly one official RFC Editor primary source, RFC 6920. Tested only whether a fixed {digest_algorithm_id,digest_bytes} evidence field can carry an unambiguous standalone digest-method identity next to digest bytes without external execution handoff. No second public source, digest computation, encoder implementation, cryptographic execution, external service, protected-primary action, manual-user execution, scheduler mutation, or other-worker/downstream/O semantic input was consumed.
observations: RFC 6920 says comparison of Named Information names is based on the digest algorithm and digest value; hashes are identical when the decoded values use the same algorithm and have the same length and binary value.
The ni URI format explicitly includes a Digest Algorithm field whose name comes from the Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry and a Digest Value field; its syntax binds alg and val together.
The binary format carries a Suite ID that specifies both hash algorithm and truncation length next to the hash value.

Section 9.4 creates the Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry with fields including optional numeric Suite ID, Hash Name String, truncation length, underlying algorithm reference, and status. Initial entries include sha-256 and several registered truncations.

Suite ID is optional, so a numeric-only digest_algorithm_id would cover only registry entries that have a Suite ID; the Hash Name String is the more general standalone identifier across registered entries.
bounded_slice.inference: Positive for the narrow schema child: RFC 6920 directly standardizes algorithm identity separately from digest bytes. A fixed evidence field can be made unambiguous by defining digest_algorithm_id as the RFC 6920 Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry Hash Name String and requiring digest_bytes length to match the registered value length/truncation. If a compact numeric field is desired, Suite ID is suitable only where the registry assigns one. This resolves identifier interpretation only; it does not prove digest computation, encoding, signing, verification, replay freshness, or algorithm suitability for a particular security purpose.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: The source notes that registry status 'current' does not itself mean an algorithm is suitable for every application. No claim is made about later registry additions or deprecations outside RFC 6920 because no second source was inspected. No implementation test established that scheduled Chat can compute, encode, sign, or verify the digest/package.
bounded_slice.replayability: A replaying reader can interpret {digest_algorithm_id,digest_bytes} without guessing the hash method when the profile fixes digest_algorithm_id to the RFC 6920 Hash Name String and validates byte length against the registered hash/truncation definition; generation and verification execution remain unresolved.
bounded_slice.hidden_executor_absence: Static specification inspection and schema binding required no external execution handoff; concrete hashing/encoding/signing/verification capabilities remain unresolved children and are not assumed.
bounded_slice.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_us: 0 for this static specification/schema slice; concrete Chat-native digest computation, deterministic encoding, COSE cryptographic execution, key trust, replay/freshness policy, PROV-to-JSON mapping, and observation/inference/uncertainty schema remain unresolved children
bounded_slice.quota_zero_assessment: The specification inspection and digest-identifier schema binding require no hosted compute, paid service, finite monthly credit, artifact store, or external API. Actual digest/cryptographic execution availability in the target Chat surface was not tested.
